title: Released off the bed
note: Used twice. The only picture in this activity where leaving the bed is correct, so the release has to be legible: she is stepping off, forward and up, toward two open welcoming hands. Everywhere else in the ladder that motion is the failure.
scene: Interior entry hall. Lucy is stepping down off her rectangular cool-grey dog bed toward the handler — front feet on the floor, back feet still on or just leaving the bed, body angled forward and up, ears lifted, plainly moving toward her and pleased about it. The handler crouches a step away with both hands open and low in front of her, palms up and empty — no treat in either hand — welcoming her in. She is smiling and relaxed. This is a release, not a recall from a distance: they are close together. The closed charcoal front door sits across the room in the background. No leash.
mustBeTrue: Lucy is clearly in the act of coming off the bed — front feet down, weight moving forward — heading toward the handler, whose hands are both open, low and empty with no treat in them.
